__**Explanation:**__

**The Accuracy of Measurement by a Try Square**

**Definition:** A try square is a precision measuring tool used predominantly in woodworking and metalworking to check the squareness or 90-degree angle between two surfaces. It ensures that two adjoining surfaces meet at a precise right angle. The accuracy of such tools is critical in precision engineering and manufacturing, as even the slightest deviation can result in errors in the final product.

**Working Principle:** The try square consists of a stock (or handle) and a blade that are fixed together at exactly 90 degrees. The measurement accuracy of a try square depends on the precision with which these components are manufactured and assembled. When the blade is placed against a surface, its alignment with the stock determines the squareness of the surface being tested.

**Factors Affecting the Accuracy of a Try Square:**

 
• The material and method of construction: A high-quality material ensures better resistance to wear and deformation over time.
 
• The precision of manufacturing: Advanced manufacturing techniques, such as grinding and lapping, enhance the accuracy of the blade and stock.
